text:
Marta (PM): Quick sync — Q2 private-deploy scope: we need to decide which customer-managed networking deltas ship in the first private distro. I sketched 3 lanes: minimal (no IPAM changes), permissive (optional CNI + manual peering), and gated (automated IPAM + route reconciliation). Thoughts?

Ajay (Eng): I prefer minimal for GA. Keep installer small, avoid extra agents. We can add a permissive checkbox for advanced installs but default should be the least surprising.

Kevin (Field Eng): +1 minimal GA. But several customers insist on automated peering. Can we offer a stable upgrade path so they can start minimal and opt-in later without re-IPing?

Marta (PM): That's the crux — upgrade path constraints. Proposal: allow in-place opt-in to permissive via a one-step config change if the cluster was provisioned with ephemeral CIDR guardrails. If not, require a migration window.

Nora (SRE): We need clear rollback semantics. If customers enable permissive and BGP flaps, support should be able to toggle back fast. Can we add a safety flag that stops advertising routes until health checks pass?

Ajay (Eng): Implementable: add a gating flag to the operator: `--peer-enabled=false` default, set to true to start peering; operator waits for local endpoints to pass a readiness probe before advertising. We'll include a short TTL on routes during the transition.

Kevin (Field Eng): For onprem customers with strict change windows, can we provide an offline migration helper that rewrites stretch CIDRs and preserves customer firewall rules?

Priya (Sales): Customers care about downtime windows. If we can promise <15m of coordination for permissive opt-in (with rollback), that's sellable. Otherwise they'd rather wait for dedicated engineering.

Marta (PM): Okay, decision leaning: ship minimal GA + permissive opt-in with operator gating and a documented offline migration path. We'll defer automated IPAM (gated lane) to post-GA.

Nora (SRE): Action item: define the health probe contract and the operator's safety timeout. I'll draft a short spec: probe interval, consecutive success threshold, route TTLs, and a manual emergency toggle.

Ajay (Eng): I will prototype the `--peer-enabled` behavior and publish a demo helm chart. ETA: 2 sprints for prototype, 1 more sprint to harden.

Kevin (Field Eng): I'll compile a runbook for onprem migration steps and customer comms templates. Also need an ipam checklist for pre-checks.

Marta (PM): Great. I'll update the product PRD with these lanes and mark gated IPAM as Q3. Also scheduling a short field working session Wed 10am to walk through the runbook. @Kevin @Ajay please bring your notes.

deploy-bot: Deployed draft runbook to #docs at https://example.internal/runbooks/privdeploy-networking-draft — reviewers: Nora, Kevin, Ajay.

Priya (Sales): Can we get a 1-pager for customers that explains the three lanes and expected downtime? I can use that in renewals conversations.

Marta (PM): Yes — I'll draft a 1-pager and circulate by EOD Friday.

Ajay (Eng): Minor tech note: for permissive opt-in we should expose a `dry-run` parameter so field can validate route assignments without advertising. Reduces risk.

Nora (SRE): +1 to `dry-run`. Also request: logs should include the reconcile step id so we can audit opt-ins per customer.

Marta (PM): Noted. Summary of decisions: 1) GA = minimal (no IPAM/auto-peering), 2) permissive opt-in via operator gating + dry-run + rollback, 3) gated automated IPAM moved to post-GA. Action owners: Ajay (peer operator prototype), Kevin (runbook & customer comms), Nora (health probe spec), Marta (PRD + 1-pager).

Kevin (Field Eng): Thanks — see you Wed 10am. :thumbsup:
